notes:
Summary / raw CRM notes: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for clinical summarization + internal support assistant. Primary concern = deterministic latency and predictable tail under production load with PHI => VPC/on-prem. SLO alignment became the central theme during tech deep-dive. Key points captured below (shorthand):

- Measurement definition: client-side end-to-end vs server-side processing. Customer insists on both: client-side p50/p95/p99 for end-to-end including LB/network (their front-end SLA), AND server-side processing time (Redwood runtime) instrumented by trace_id for root-cause.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: need separate SLOs. Streaming: define two metrics -> time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and event-inter-chunk p99 (stability). Non-streaming (batch/generation): define full-response latency p50/p95/p99.
- Target numbers discussed (customer asks for examples to calibrate procurement):
    * Non-streaming (end-to-end): p50 ~ 80ms, p95 ~ 300ms, p99 ~ 800ms for median summary requests (avg prompt 512 tokens).
    * Streaming (first-byte): p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 400ms. Event pacing (subsequent chunks) p95 < 100ms.
    * Server-only processing budget: allow 20-30% of end-to-end for network/proxy overhead; Redwood to provide server-side p50/p95/p99 broken out.
- Measurement windows & aggregation: 5m sliding windows for realtime alerting, 1h/24h windows for SLA reporting. Use client side tags (client_ts, request_id, trace_id) so we can correlate.
- Instrumentation requirements: request_id, trace_id, model_version, sequence_length, token_count, streaming_flag, region, backend_node. Customer wants JSON webhook for each SLA breach and daily aggregated report.
- Synthetic vs replay traffic: POC will run mixed workload: 30% streaming chat, 50% single-shot summarization, 20% embeddings + reranking. Need to replay production token length distribution (they shared sample histogram).
- Throughput & reserved GPU planning: for their 95k tokens/sec steady-state (90% non-streaming), initial recommendation: 6x A100-40GB equiv nodes dedicated, with 2x burst nodes for traffic spikes; autoscale disabled in reserved pool but burst allowed via overflow pool. Redwood suggested capacity model based on concurrency and tokens/sec; customer requested a deterministic mapping: tokens/sec -> reserved GPUs -> expected p95. We'll produce a lookup table in POC.
- SLA negotiation items: failure budget (monthly) for p99 <= 0.2% default; credits table (pro-rata) if missed; maintenance blackout windows (customer requires 4h/month max); scheduled upgrades needs 48h notice and optional canary rollouts.
- Reporting & observability: they want per-route model dashboards, raw traces for incidents, and an exportable CSV for p50/p95/p99 per hour. Redwood Console features appealed to them.
- Acceptance criteria for POC: 72h steady-state run with production token distro, server-side p99 <= agreed threshold (baseline 800ms) for non-streaming, first-byte streaming p95 <= 150ms, no data residency leaks, security questionnaire passed.
- Quote from CTO (paraphrase): "We can tolerate a bit of median variance but need repeatable tail behavior—p99 is the business metric for user trust."

Actionables recorded in CRM: produce POC runbook (Priya), detailed GPU capacity lookup table, draft SLA with credits/maintenance windows, instrumented POC harness that writes both client-side and server-side timing into logs for correlation. Procurement wants pricing + draft SLA by 2026-03-20.
